newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain court to issue Gonzalez "dirty war" ruling.
newsitem.headline: Spain court to issue Gonzalez "dirty war" ruling.

text.p: Spain's Supreme Court will rule on November 4 whether to question former Socialist prime minister Felipe Gonzalez, either as a witness or as a suspect, in investigations into a "dirty war" against Basque separatists, court sources said on Friday.

Gonzalez has been accused by the conservative Popular Party government's number two, Francisco Alvarez Cascos, of masterminding a campaign of killing, torture and kidnapping from 1983 to 1987 in which 28 people died. One third were killed by mistake.
Gonzalez has denied any role in the illegal operations aimed at ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) rebels.

The Socialists, in power for 13 years, were defeated in elections in March after rapidly losing popularity over "dirty war" allegations and other corruption scandals. But the accusations have continued to hound Gonzalez as leader of the opposition.

Alvarez Cascos now controls Spain's secret services and has unmatched access to secret information. Former security chiefs have also said Gonzalez authorised the self-styled Anti-Terrorist Liberation Groups (GAL) death squads.

A former Socialist interior minister, Jose Barrionuevo, is already on trial before the Supreme Court on charges of creating and funding the GAL. ETA has killed about 800 people since 1968 in their drice for an independent Basque state.
